expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: You're using training to control an operator that sometimes ignores training. Caps and repetition are still rung-zero instructions

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: Keep CLAUDE.md for facts—where generated code comes from, and how to regenerate it—not rules you need the agent to obey

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
expectations.evidence: Shows deny array with Bash and Edit/Write patterns with wildcards

expectations.text: Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: Force-push also needs a PreToolUse hook: permission patterns are prefix matches, so they can miss forms such as git push origin main --force

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: give it a useful refusal [message with what to do]; the message tells Claude what to do

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: Then prove the device: Attempt a force push; confirm it is denied and the message tells Claude what to do

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: Put this in committed .claude/settings.json, not settings.local.json, so every clone gets it

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: You're using training to control an operator that sometimes ignores training
